complexity.correctness_reason: Float division of arrival times loses exactness once target and speed are unbounded: two fleets whose arrival times agree to 53 significant bits but differ beyond that get merged into one, which NeetCode's caps (values <= 10^6) can never trigger.
complexity.notes: The guard threshold uses n * bit_length(n) as a cheap stand-in for n log n, which is fine. Under the benchmark scaling (target = 2n+1) the counting branch is always taken, so it runs in O(n). One robustness issue: arrival times are compared as floats, so once target/speed grow past double precision the comparison can be wrong — comparing (target - p1) * s2 >= (target - p2) * s1 with cross-multiplied integers is exact at any magnitude. Minor style points: the AI-attribution comment is best removed, and the sort branch could iterate the sorted list in reverse instead of relying on pop() from the end.
complexity.summary: A guarded hybrid: if target is smaller than roughly n log n the cars are ordered by a counting array indexed by position, otherwise by a plain sort; then a single right-to-left sweep compares each car's arrival time against the current lead fleet's and counts a new fleet whenever a car arrives strictly later.
